contexts.text: A small globe on a pyramidal base, which (the deceitful) suppose to be the universe, under their government... They believe themselves to be the gods of the universe. AC 1506:end. AC 1749:2.
Some come to them, as they expressed it, from the universe.
Everyone acknowledges a Supreme Being when he beholds the universe...
Spirits can, by phantasy, be translated in a moment... as it were from one end of the universe to the other.
(The love of self causes them) to want to exercise command over the universe... AC 2219:4.
As a King, the Lord governs each and all things in the universe from Divine truth; and as a Priest, from Divine good.
In all His combats of temptations, the Lord fought... for all in the universe.

Whatever appears in the universe is a representative of the Lord's Kingdom, insomuch that there is nothing in the atmospheric and stelliferous universe, or in the Earth and its three kingdoms, which is not, in its own way, representative. Explained.
It follows that the visible universe is nothing else than a theatre representative of the Lord's Kingdom...

The radiant circle is the Divine from Him, which inflows not only into Heaven, but also into the universe... Aristotle added, that He who disposes and rules Heaven, also disposes and rules the universe...
When this idea was unfolded... there was manifested as it were a universe leading to the Lord; and... so it is with every idea of what is good and true.
The Spirits of Mercury are allowed to wander about, and acquire Knowledges of Things which are in the universe. AC 6925.
There are Earths with men in them, not only in this system, but also in the universe, in immense numbers. AC 6927.
Men may believe that there are more Earths in the universe than one, from the fact that the visible universe, resplendent with innumerable stars, is so immense.
The visible universe is a means for the coming forth of Earths...
Two statues which appear at the terminus of the created universe, which are said to swallow those who think of what the Divine was doing before the creation. (Compare TCR 31:end.)
He conceives an idea of the Divine from the visible universe without an end, or with an end in obscurity.
By changes of state. Angels and Spirits can be translated... even to the Earths which are at the end of the universe...
Subtitle. On the Earths in the Universe.
The created universe, regarded from order, is so full of wisdom from love that...
That all things in the universe have been created from the Divine love and Divine wisdom of God Man. General article.
This appears from the correspondence of all things in the universe with all things of man... insomuch that it may be said that man also is a kind of universe. Explained.
In the Spiritual World (all objects) appear around those there in just such an aspect as that of the created universe...

(Thus) the created universe is an image representative of God Man; and it is His love and wisdom which are presented in the universe in an image. Not that the created universe is God Man; but that it is from Him; for nothing whatever in the created universe is substance and form in itself, or life in itself, or love and wisdom in itself.
That all things in the created universe are recipients of the Divine love and Divine wisdom of God Man. General article.
Hence the universe, with each and all things of it, is called in the Word the work of the hands of Jehovah.
Therefore the universe, which is an image of God, and consequently full of God, could not be created except in God from God, (and not from nothing). Explained.
That all the other things of the universe, which are not like Angels and men, are also recipients... Explained.
(Thus) the Divine is in each and all things of the created universe; and hence it is that the created Universe is the work of the hands of Jehovah. Explained.

Although the Divine is in each and all things of the created universe, still there is nothing of the Divine in itself in the esse of them; for the created universe is not God, but is from God; and, because it is from God, His image is in it. Explained.

I have heard many say that they are willing to acknowledge that the Divine is in each and all things of the universe, because they see the marvellous things of God in them... yet when they heard that the Divine is actually in each and all things of the created universe, they were indignant...
That there is a relation to man of all things of the created universe...
God is a Man; and the created universe is His image. Explained.
That the Divine infills all spaces of the universe without space. General article.
That the Lord created the universe and all things of it by the medium of the (spiritual) Sun... General article.

End, cause, and effect... exist in the greatest, that is, in the universe, in the following order. In the Sun... is the end of all things; in the Spiritual World are their causes; and in the natural world are their effects.
Under Create, see this reference. DLW 156. DLW 283. DLW 284. DLW 303:end. DLW 326:end. DLW 329. DLW 349:end. DP 9. DP 51. DP 202. DP 324:2. CL 380:end. TCR 46.
The universe in general has been distinguished into two worlds: the Spiritual, and the natural...

In the created universe, in both its greatests and its leasts, are... end, cause, and effect. The reason these three are in the greatest and least things of the created universe, is that they are in God the Creator... And hence it is that the universe, which has been created from His Esse, and which, regarded as to uses, is His image, has obtained these three in each and all things of it.
The greatest things in which there are degrees of both kinds, are the universe in its whole complex; the natural world in its complex; and the Spiritual World in its...
The perfection of the created universe is from the similitude of the generals and of the particulars, or of the greatest and least things, as to these degrees...
That the Lord from eternity... created the universe and all things of it from Himself, and not from nothing. General article. DLW 285:3, Explained.
They feared that thus they might come strongly into the thought that the created universe is God because from God...
That the Lord from eternity... could not have created the universe and all things of it, unless He were a Man. General article. DLW 286.
They think, How can God as a Man wander all over the universe, from space to space, and create? Explained.
That the Lord from eternity... produced from Himself the Sun of the Spiritual World; and from it created the universe and all things of it. General article. ISB 5. TCR 33.

That all the uses in the created universe correspond to the uses (in man), will be demonstrated. (For) God as a Man is the very form itself of all uses; from which form all the uses in the created universe derive their origin; and thus the created universe, regarded as to uses, is His image.

All uses... have a relation to all things of man... and therefore man is the universe in a kind of image; and, conversely, the universe, regarded as to uses, is man in an image. DLW 319, General article.
Man has been called a microcosm... from the fact that he bears relation to the macrocosm, which is the universe in its whole complex. Explained.
The ancients called man a microcosm, or little universe, from their knowledge of correspondences. Explained. DLW 320. Explained.
The idea of the universe as regarded in the Spiritual World. DLW 321, Explained.
(Thus) the universe of the Spiritual World is exactly like the universe of the natural world, with the sole difference that the things there are not fixed and stated...
That the universe of that World bears relation, in an image, to man...
From this they know there that... the created universe, regarded as to uses, is an image of God.
Hence it is that man is as it were a universe... in the least form.
That the universe with each and all things of it has been created from the Divine love through the Divine wisdom. General article.
A sphere for the conservation of the created universe (proceeds from Him). CL 386, Explained.
The multitude of those who believe that nature has created the universe...
For everything that proceeds from the Lord goes through the universe in an instant.
That unless God were One, the universe could not have been created and preserved. General article.
Otherwise, that whole universe, into which Souls go... might be drawn through the eye of a needle... This would be possible if there were no substantial extense there.

(Thus) the universe is a work cohering from primes to ultimates, because it is a work containant of ends, causes, and effects in an indissoluble connection... and it follows that the universe is a work containant of the Divine love, the Divine wisdom, and Uses...

That the universe consists of perpetual uses produced by wisdom and initiated by love, may be seen by every wise man... when he acquires a general idea of the creation of the universe, and in it views the particulars...
(Thus) the universe has been created by God in order that uses may come forth; and therefore the universe may be called a theatre of uses...
God created the universe from Himself as Order, in order, for order.
On the creation of the universe. Chapter. (See Create. TCR 76. TCR 78. TCR 79.)
From the belief that nature is the creatress of the universe, it follows that the universe is that which is called God...

When I was extracting what is said in  about the universal devastation, evil Genii and Spirits could not desist from the cupidity of exaggerating what is there said... insomuch that they grieved that the universe would not be destroyed.
In this way communications are instituted... even if they were in another universe.
For the ideas were determined into the universe, and were thus dissipated...
That the universe is governed by the Lord... very easily. Explained.
They said that they are carried to the ends of the universe.
That the general life of the Lord inflows into the universe.
He was so inflated as to fill the universe...
He was told that [he was] at the ends of the universe.
On the inhabitants of another world, or of some universe, in the starry heaven. General article. SE 3296.
The Spirits of Mercury were present... as it appeared to me, near the end of this universe.
Could they conceive of anything as existing beyond the bounds of the universe? or whether there is any space outside the universe?

Those who had been in such a phantasy, seem to themselves to be withdrawn outside the universe, (where) some of them said that it was well with them... being remote from the troubles which exist in the created universe. But, being kept in the phantasy that they were outside the universe... they reasoned about that non-space outside the universe, that it is without end; and therefore they seemed to themselves to advance still further, until at last they saw some there who spoke to them... saying that they are in the boundary outside the universe, and that they themselves are the bounds; and that if they approached them they would swallow them. In this way they struck terror into them to prevent their advancing further... Those in the bounds were a kind of statues. Described.
Thus the universe, as to its inmosts and to its outmosts, is organic, the Lord alone being the Life, of that the universe is full of the Lord.
(The lascivious girls) receded at last to the ends of the universe...
When some one was absent at the ends of the universe...
They who have thought that there is a beginning to all things... are at the end of the universe.
(The Nephilim) bent their cavernous way... even to the limits of this universe, and... were cast into as it were a stagnant sea, in another universe.
She was then conveyed outside the universe, to the left... but she changed the sphere of the other universe...
I wondered who those were in the middle boundary, between this world and the universe.
On a certain people in the universe, and Charles XII General article.
There was another Society in the universe...
From these two the universe was created; and therefore all things in the universe bear relation to good and truth.
The creation of the universe cannot be better seen than from its types in the Heavens; there, creation is perpetual and instantaneous. Described. (Continued. See Create.)
2. The human mind... can see that the universe has been created by God.

5. 3. A summary of the arcana of creation. The Sun of Heaven, in which is the Lord, is the common centre of the universe; and all things of the universe are circumferences and circumferences, even to the last one; and these the Lord rules from Himself alone as one continuous thing; but the mediate ones from the ultimate one; and He animates and actuates these unceasingly, as easily as a man, from his understanding and will, animates and actuates his body... (Ang. Idea: quoted under Create.)
God. 6. On the creation of the universe by the one and infinite God, from Divine love, through Divine wisdom.
God. 6. 6. The created universe consists of infinite receptacles of these three.
God. 6. 7. The created universe is a receptacle of uses, which, from their origin, are infinite.
God. 6. 8. It follows that the created universe is the fulness of God.
God. 8. Unless each and all things in the world and Heaven bore relation to a One, who is, lives, and has power of Himself, the universe would be dissipated in a moment.
